Project Architecture

This report details the implementation of a real-time signal classification pipeline that converts raw sensor data into motor commands. The architecture consists of four stages:

  • Signal Preprocessing: A 4th-order Butterworth bandpass filter (20–450 Hz) removes environmental noise and motion artifacts. Signals are then normalized with StandardScaler.
  • Window Segmentation: The continuous datastream is segmented into 200-sample windows with 50-sample overlap. Each window is assigned the majority class label.
  • Feature Engineering: Four time-domain features (RMS, MAV, ZCR, WL) are extracted per channel, yielding 16 features per window.
  • Classification: A Random Forest classifier (200 trees, stratified 80/20 split) identifies one of five grip patterns: rest, power_grip, pinch, lateral, and point.
